messages:
alex: Heads-up — sample app (JS SDK) fails on both Deno and Bun. Importing the SDK in Deno gives `TypeError: crypto.subtle is undefined`, and Bun throws `Cannot find module '@redwood/inference'` for an ESM import. Anyone else hit this today?

maria: Yep saw a stack from QA earlier. Which SDK build are you using (dist vs deno bundle)?

alex: Using `@redwood/inference@0.8.2` from npm. App entry: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'`. Error in Bun: `Error: Cannot find module` at resolve step. Deno error is at runtime when calling `new RedwoodClient(...)` — webcrypto missing.

sam: Bun's resolver is weird for packages without a clear `exports`/`browser` field. Quick check: does the package ship a deno/edge entrypoint in `package.json`? If not Bun may try to resolve `main` (cjs) which fails.

ida: For webcrypto on Deno — Deno has `globalThis.crypto.subtle` but some CI images are old. Which Deno version? Older Deno needed `--unstable` for some apis.

alex: Deno 1.36.0 on CI. The local dev machine (1.44) works. CI pinned to earlier image. Good catch.

maria: Two separate issues then: resolver + runtime env. For Bun, temporary workaround is to import the ESM entry directly (we ship `dist/esm/index.mjs`). Example: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.mjs'` — ugly but it worked in my repro.

sam: We should also add `exports` map to package.json to point `./deno` and `./edge` entrypoints. That avoids consumers needing to guess. Also verify `type: \"module\"` so Bun uses ESM resolution.

ida: For Deno CI, either bump the base image or detect and polyfill webcrypto. Quick polyfill pattern I used in another project: `if (!globalThis.crypto?.subtle) { globalThis.crypto = await import('https://deno.land/std@0.195.0/node/crypto.ts').then(m=>m.webcrypto) }` — not ideal but works for older runners.

alex: Nice. For TS types, Deno complained about `Buffer` references in the SDK types (coming from some dependency). That breaks `deno check`.

maria: We can publish a deno-typed `.d.ts` that avoids Node-only types and reference it from the deno entrypoint. Or ship types with conditional exports: `types` + `types.deno`.

sam: Actionable list: 1) Add `exports` map with `deno`/`edge`/`import` keys 2) Publish a small `dist/deno/mod.ts` that re-exports SDK but is Deno-compatible 3) Add a runtime check for `globalThis.crypto` + documented polyfill 4) Add note in quickstart about Bun import quirks + direct esm path.

ida: I'll open a tiny PR for the polyfill + docs. We should also add a CI job that runs `deno check` on the deno entrypoint and installs Bun resolution smoke tests.

alex: Thanks! I posted a minimal repro in the repo under `examples/deno-bun-repro` (linked in the ticket). Devs: if you have a sec, please try local `bun` with `bun --version` (I used 1.0.10) and report back.

maria: One more gotcha: some consumers import from `@redwood/inference` without suffix and bundlers pick the `module` field. We should ensure the `module` field points to an actual ESM file (no CJS shims). Otherwise Bun gets the wrong file.

sam: Agreed — also add small CI that runs `node --input-type=module` style smoke test or `bun run` on the example app.

dev-bot: Ticket created: RN-1234 — \"deno/bun SDK compatibility: exports map, deno entry, webcrypto polyfill, types\" (assigned to ida). :white_check_mark:

ida: I'll start the PR with `package.json` export map + `dist/deno/mod.ts` and add a note to quickstart for Bun + Deno. Will ping here when ready. :rocket:
